N-2.9-A.skill: order logarithms with different bases and arguments by estimating each value against benchmarks, rather than by the size of the base or the argument alone.

N-2.9-B.skill: solve a nested logarithmic equation by undoing the outer logarithm first and then the inner one, keeping track of which base goes with which step.

N-2.10-A.skill: evaluate the inverse of a shifted and scaled exponential function at a given output by undoing the shift, the scale, and then the exponential in order.

N-2.10-B.skill: determine the domain and asymptote of an inverse exponential function from the range and horizontal asymptote of the original, including reflected and shifted cases.

N-2.11-A.skill: describe increasing or decreasing behavior, concavity, and the vertical asymptote of a transformed logarithmic function from its equation, including a reflection.

N-2.11-B.skill: interpret the coefficient of a logarithmic model as a change per multiplication of the input, and find the factor that produces a given increase in the output.

N-2.12-A.skill: decide which logarithm-property rewrite is valid for every x in the domain of the original expression, recognizing that a power rule applied to an even power needs an absolute value.

N-2.12-B.skill: write the logarithm of a quotient involving a root in terms of given logarithms, using log₁₀(5) = 1 − log₁₀(2) and the product, quotient and power properties.

N-2.13-A.skill: solve a logarithmic inequality by combining the exponential rewrite with the domain requirement that the argument is positive, and by checking when the inequality direction reverses.

N-2.13-B.skill: model when two exponential quantities become equal and write the solution time as a logarithmic expression, handling both growth and decay.

N-2.14-A.skill: use residuals (observed minus predicted) from a logarithmic model to decide where, and by how much, the model overestimates the data.

N-2.14-B.skill: compare average rates of change of a logarithmic model on two intervals that each span one multiplication of the input, and interpret why the rate slows.

N-2.15-A.skill: recover the exponential model y = a·bˣ from two points on a semi-log line, using the slope for b and the vertical intercept (as an exponent) for a.

N-2.15-B.skill: interpret the slope of a semi-log line as growth per unit of time and use it to find a doubling or tripling time.
